components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary call-to-action. Used for 'Sign in', 'Create', 'Add Transaction', 'Save'.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; background: oklch(0.40 0.06 260); color: oklch(0.97 0.005 260); font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; border: none; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, opacity 0.15s; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px oklch(0.40 0.06 260); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.22 0.025 15); font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; border: 1px solid oklch(0.90 0.015 25); border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; white-space: nowrap; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: oklch(0.95 0.018 20); color: oklch(0.30 0.03 15); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px oklch(0.40 0.06 260); } .ds-btn-outline:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; background: oklch(0.56 0.15 22); color: oklch(0.99 0.005 30); font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; border: none; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.15s; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px oklch(0.40 0.06 260); } .ds-btn-destructive:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

narrative.overview:
Budgeteer's interface is a cosy, ordered workspace where the numbers do the talking. Like a well-worn leather-bound ledger in a quiet study: warm parchment tones, a cool slate blue accent, and typography that feels crafted but never precious. The palette pairs warm rose-tinted neutrals with a cool primary accent for a sophisticated warm/cool contrast. The primary accent is user-customizable from Settings, defaulting to slate blue.

The product register means this is a tool first. Users sit down to log a transaction, review spending, or invite a household member — and the UI should disappear into that task, warmly.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutral palette (rose-tinted) paired with a cool slate blue primary accent — intentional warm/cool contrast.
Dual-font system: Lora (serif) for headings gives a cosy, editorial feel; DM Sans (humanist sans) for body ensures fast, legible scanning.
Flat by default, layered with purpose: tonal stacking for depth; shadows reserved for interactive states and modals.
User-customizable accent color persisted to the backend (Settings page).
Generous whitespace (24px padding on cards, 24px sidebar padding, 24px page margins) punctuated by dense data rows.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit on the same z-plane until an interaction or structural need lifts them. Sidebars and content panels are distinguished by background color and a 1px border, not by a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Accent Rarity Rule
rules.body: The primary accent (slate blue by default, customizable) is used on no more than 10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Font Role Rule
rules.body: Lora is for headings (h1-h3) only. DM Sans is for everything else. Neither font crosses into the other's role.

rules.name: The Fixed Income/Expense Rule
rules.body: Income and expense colors (sage green / muted terracotta) are fixed semantic signals. They do not change with the user's accent preference.

dos: Do use the warm rose-tinted neutrals consistently paired with the cool primary accent.
Do use Lora for headings (h1-h3) and DM Sans for body — this pairing is intentional and must stay consistent.
Do keep income/expense colors (sage green / muted terracotta) fixed — they are semantic signals, not accent-linked.
Do keep all interactive elements at 36px height for consistent touch targets.
Do verify muted-foreground (oklch(0.48 0.025 15)) against background for 4.5:1 minimum contrast.
Do use focus-visible:ring-1 ring-ring on every interactive element.
Do keep form error messages as text below the field. Do not change the input border to red.
Do skeleton-load content areas with the same surface tokens. No spinners.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: replace all animated transitions with instant (0ms) state changes.
Do verify all color pairs in dark mode meet the same contrast ratios as light mode.
Do persist the user's theme preference to localStorage so the choice survives page reload.
Do default to the system prefers-color-scheme on first visit.
donts: Don't use gradient text, colored accent stripes (border-left greater than 1px), or glassmorphism. Prohibited entirely.
Don't add decorative motion. Motion conveys state only (hover, focus, open, close) and stays within 150-250ms.
Don't use modals as the first thought for interaction. Exhaust inline and progressive disclosure patterns first.
Don't use the primary accent on more than 10% of any single screen. Its rarity is the point.
Don't create different button shapes or input styles on different pages. The component vocabulary is universal.
Don't show 'you're offline' banners that block interaction. A subtle indicator in the sidebar footer is sufficient.
Don't use cards inside cards. A card is the outermost container; use direct child elements for internal grouping.
Don't override the font pairing — DM Sans on body, Lora on headings. Neither font should appear in the other's role.
